## Amboró National Park: the forests of eastern Bolivia

Amboró is a national park in eastern Bolivia, where the Andes meet lower-lying natural areas. Humid forests, mountain slopes, river valleys and diverse bird communities can all be found here. For visitors, the attraction is walking through nature and experiencing a side of Bolivia very different from the dry Altiplano.

Amboró can be incorporated into a journey around [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/) and [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/). However, it is a large protected area with several approaches. Your departure point determines which section of forest is accessible and how long the journey takes.

## Why the forests of Amboró are interesting

On humid-forest trails, plants, birds and surrounding scenery are the principal attractions. Depending on the sector, you may see dense vegetation, towering trees, mountain slopes and small streams. Some paths cross uneven terrain and require suitable footwear.

Wildlife watching depends on the time of day, weather and human activity. Photographs of rare species in promotional material do not mean every animal will be encountered on a particular walk. If birds are your priority, a quiet route and knowledgeable guide matter more than the number of stops.

## Can Amboró be combined with Samaipata?

Samaipata is known for the El Fuerte archaeological complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It allows travellers to combine ancient history with a walk in a natural setting.

Nevertheless, [El Fuerte archaeological site](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) and Amboró National Park are **two different places**. Visiting one does not automatically include an excursion to the other. For the nature outing, select a particular trail and access point; for the archaeological programme, allow time to explore the rock monument.

## Preparing for a forest walk

Because of the humid climate, forest paths can be slippery. Comfortable enclosed shoes, drinking water and rain protection make the day easier. Avoid venturing onto an unfamiliar trail without guidance, especially in difficult weather or when water crossings are involved.

Protected-area visitor rules and access restrictions apply to certain sections. Do not leave paths, feed wildlife or drop litter. The authorised guides and current park regulations determine the exact visiting format.

| Plan | What to check |
|---|---|
| Walking | Trail and difficulty |
| Birdwatching | Area and time |
| Excursion from the city | Road and transport |
| Conservation | Access rules |

## Amboró on a Bolivia journey

Unlike the open high-altitude landscapes of [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) or the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), Amboró introduces visitors to the forest ecosystems of eastern Bolivia. Combining these regions requires substantial transfers and different accommodation arrangements.

When browsing [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/), compare actual routes and whether nature excursions are included. Check which part of the park is visited, how long the walk lasts and what guiding is provided.

## Frequently asked questions about Amboró National Park

### Where is Amboró?

In eastern Bolivia, where the Andes transition towards more humid forest regions, relatively close to the Santa Cruz area.

### Can you see animals in Amboró?

The park is home to many birds and mammals, but sightings depend on the particular route and natural conditions. They are not guaranteed.

### Is the park suitable for an independent walk?

Check the rules and requirements for guidance in the sector you plan to visit. A local guide is advisable on an unfamiliar forest trail.

### Are Amboró and El Fuerte in Samaipata the same site?

No. El Fuerte is an archaeological monument; Amboró is a protected natural area with forest trails.

## Tours through Amboró National Park: what is included

If you would like to see [Amboró National Park](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/) in Bolivia, start by considering the scale of the journey. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a compulsory park visit: [Bolivia in 12 Days: All Excursions with Guides](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/). This multi-day tour through Bolivia combines Amboró's cloud forest with historic cities, Uyuni Salt Flat and Lake Titicaca.

Amboró is part of the **main itinerary**, not an optional outing. After breakfast on day 3, travellers head for the cloud forest, walking among local plants and large ferns. In the afternoon they return to [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/), stopping at [Cuevas Waterfalls](/bolivia/place/cuevas-waterfalls/) along the way.

There are currently no short, standalone Amboró-only trips in this selection. If the park walk is your main goal, consider whether the entire 12-day journey matches the time you want to spend in Bolivia, and read the [detailed 12-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/).

## How Amboró connects with Samaipata and Santa Cruz

The eastern part of the journey follows a clear sequence: first Santa Cruz, then [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) and its El Fuerte archaeological complex, followed by Amboró's natural scenery and the waterfalls. In the first few days, travellers therefore experience both historical monuments and humid Andean foothill forests. The journey then continues towards [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/) and higher-altitude regions.

| Stage | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Day 1: [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/) | City tour |
| Day 2: [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) | El Fuerte complex |
| Day 3: [Amboró](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/) | Cloud forest and [Cuevas](/bolivia/place/cuevas-waterfalls/) |
| From day 4 | Sucre, Potosí, Uyuni and the Andes |

The benefit of this sequence is that eastern Bolivia's forests have a dedicated place in the itinerary. Rather than simply passing the forest area on the way from the airport, travellers devote an excursion day to it. The journey then moves beyond the green foothills to highland scenery on the same trip.

## What to expect from a cloud-forest visit

Amboró is a protected natural area managed by the Bolivian service SERNAP. The park is known for its forest ecosystems and rich plant life. Its forests are markedly different from the dry highland landscapes travellers will encounter later.

**This tour includes a cloud-forest walk and observations of vegetation.** It does not promise sightings of particular wild animals, a lengthy trek or visits to every sector of the national park. Activities in Amboró must comply with protected-area rules and designated visitor zones; the actual route depends on access permissions and natural conditions.

Take shoes with good grip, water and rain protection on this excursion day. Humid-forest paths may be slippery. The tour description does not specify the precise walking distance or difficulty, so discuss them before booking, especially if travelling with children or needing an easier walk.

## Who will enjoy the 12-day route with Amboró?

This tour suits travellers who want to see several different parts of Bolivia in one journey. After the eastern section, the itinerary includes [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/), Potosí, [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), high-altitude lagoons and Lake Titicaca. Amboró adds forest landscapes to a route that would otherwise largely focus on the Andes and salt flats.

If you are interested only in Amboró, the full 12-day tour may be more than you need. If [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the lagoons matter most, begin with the [Bolivia tour catalogue](/bolivia/tour/), which has routes with different geographical emphases. For both forest and Andes, this programme joins the two without requiring you to organise every domestic transfer.

The [12-day programme page](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) specifies accommodation, excursion transport, admission tickets and guide arrangements. Air tickets and lunches or dinners not listed in the meal plan are excluded. These conditions belong to that particular published tour, not to every possible trip to the park.

## Frequently asked questions about Amboró tours

### On which day do travellers visit Amboró?

On the Ada Tours 12-day itinerary, it is **day 3**. After the cloud-forest walk, Cuevas Waterfalls and a return to Santa Cruz are planned. The preceding day is devoted to Samaipata.

### Is Amboró included in the main programme or an extra?

The park is on the main route of this tour. The day description and general conditions appear on the [programme page](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/). No separate one-day product is currently featured in this selection.

### Do I need to prepare for a strenuous hike?

The itinerary promises a cloud-forest walk, but specifies neither a trail length nor a difficulty grade. Check the duration and trail characteristics if you need to assess exertion.

### Can visitors see animals in Amboró?

The park protects diverse ecosystems, but encounters with particular animals on this excursion are not guaranteed. The confirmed activities focus on forest walking and vegetation.

### What else can be visited nearby?

This stage also includes [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) and [Cuevas Waterfalls](/bolivia/place/cuevas-waterfalls/). Explore other routes in the [Bolivia tour catalogue](/bolivia/tour/).

## The Stone Tree in Bolivia: why this rock resembles a tree

The [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/), known as *Árbol de Piedra*, is a solitary rock formation in the open [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) of southwestern Bolivia. A narrow lower section supports a massive, irregular top. Its outline resembles both a tree and a stone mushroom, making it easy to recognise among the other rocks of the Altiplano.

A stop by the rock usually takes up a small part of a jeep journey. The appeal is examining the effects of weathering at close quarters and seeing the austere high-altitude landscape around it. There is no forest of stone trees here, nor a separate lengthy walking trail that visitors must follow.

## How the unusual shape formed

The Stone Tree's shape is attributed to weathering and erosion in a dry, windy environment. Sand particles carried close to the ground by the wind act especially strongly on the lower part of a rock. Over time, the base narrows while the broader upper section remains.

This creates a **rock pedestal or stone mushroom**, a natural geological formation requiring no human intervention. Other isolated volcanic rocks occur in the Siloli Desert, but the Stone Tree has the most recognisable silhouette. Tourist publications disagree on its exact height, so it is better not to choose a journey based on a claimed measurement.

## Where the rock is and what to see nearby

The Stone Tree stands in the high-altitude Siloli Desert, near routes through [Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). This remote part of the Bolivian Altiplano is usually reached by four-wheel-drive vehicle.

On a journey through southwestern Bolivia, it is often linked with a series of highland lagoons: [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) and [Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/). Each stop offers something different. At lagoons, travellers observe water, shorelines and birds; at the Stone Tree, they see one striking example of how wind works upon rock.

The route may then continue towards [Ollagüe Volcano](/bolivia/place/ollague-volcano/) and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Having the Stone Tree on an itinerary does not mean every nearby location is automatically included.

## Which Ada Tours trips visit the Stone Tree?

On the [three-day Uyuni jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the rock is visited on day 2. After the high-altitude lagoons, the vehicle crosses Siloli to the Stone Tree, then continues towards Ollagüe Volcano and Puerto Chuvica. That night is spent at a hotel built from salt.

On the [11-day Bolivia journey](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/), the Stone Tree is part of a route through the Siloli Desert, after which the itinerary goes to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), geysers and other natural sights. The longer trip also includes Titicaca, La Paz and Torotoro.

The same site can therefore feature on a short jeep expedition or an extensive journey across Bolivia. Compare the full sequence of days, not just the name of the shared stop.

## What to consider at this high-altitude stop

Siloli is high in the Andes. Exposed winds, strong sunshine and large differences between daytime and night-time temperatures require warm layered clothing, sunglasses and water. Altitude affects travellers differently; allow time to acclimatise, particularly after arriving from lowlands.

Approach the rock according to your guide's instructions and protect its fragile shape: do not climb onto its base, chip off stone or leave inscriptions. For photographs, a safe viewing position that also captures the surrounding scenery is sufficient.

## Frequently asked questions about the Stone Tree

### Was the Stone Tree made by people?

No. It is a natural rock formation shaped by prolonged weathering and windblown sand.

### Can I drive there from Uyuni in an ordinary car?

The Stone Tree is usually visited in a four-wheel-drive vehicle on a route through the Siloli Desert and lagoons. Road conditions and season are important when choosing transport.

### Is it the same place as the Valley of Rocks?

No. The [Valley of Rocks near Alota](/bolivia/place/valley-of-rocks-alota/) is a different area with numerous rock formations. The Stone Tree is one specific recognisable rock in the Siloli Desert.

### How much time should be spent at the Stone Tree?

It is generally a stop during a jeep excursion day, not a multi-day destination by itself. Duration depends on the overall programme and weather.

## Which tours visit the Stone Tree in Bolivia?

The [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) is a rock formation in the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), near the natural areas of [Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Its unusual shape formed through weathering and wind erosion: the rock's base is narrower than its top. On journeys through southwestern Bolivia, the stop is usually combined with lagoons, volcanoes and salt flats.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting the Stone Tree on the main itinerary. Choose according to the length of the entire journey, its starting point and the other regions covered. **Stopping at the rock is only one short episode in a larger high-altitude road journey.** These programmes are not designed as trips solely to the Stone Tree.

## A short option: three-day jeep tour of southwestern Bolivia

[Uyuni Salt Flat Jeep Tour in Three Days: Lagoons, Geysers and Volcanoes](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) focuses on Altiplano nature. It is a group route lasting three days and two nights. The journey begins at the Hito Cajones border point, with the Stone Tree visited on **day 2**.

That day, the road passes [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) and [Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), crosses the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) and reaches the rock. The itinerary then continues to [Ollagüe Volcano](/bolivia/place/ollague-volcano/). On other days, travellers visit [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), geothermal areas and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

**Best for:** travellers who want to dedicate several days to southwestern Bolivia by jeep and see its natural sights without a lengthy city itinerary. This is not an ordinary day trip from central Uyuni with a return the same evening: check the starting point and sequence of stops on the [specific tour page](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). Admission to Eduardo Avaroa Reserve and Incahuasi Island is paid for separately.

## An extended 11-day Bolivia journey

[Bolivia in 11 Days: Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni and Torotoro](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) is suitable if you want to explore more of the country than its salt flats. The itinerary combines [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), La Paz, archaeological sites, Uyuni, lagoons and the natural areas of Torotoro.

The Stone Tree is included on **day 7**. After the stop in the Siloli Desert, travellers continue to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the Sol de Mañana geothermal field, [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) and Laguna Verde.

**Best for:** travellers interested in both Bolivian culture and its mountainous landscapes. The Stone Tree accounts for a short part of a busy day, but the overall journey covers many more regions. When choosing between the compact jeep tour and the 11-day programme, the key question is whether you want to concentrate on the southwest or explore Bolivia more widely.

## Peru and Bolivia in 15 days: the Stone Tree on an international route

[Peru and Bolivia: Uyuni and Altiplano Lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) combines historic and natural sites in two countries. The Peruvian section includes Lima, Cusco and Machu Picchu; the Bolivian portion includes Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni and high-altitude lagoons.

The Stone Tree appears on **day 11**, devoted to Eduardo Avaroa's natural sights. The route passes through Siloli, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), Sol de Mañana, hot springs and the Laguna Verde area. The rock remains one stop, not the sole purpose of the day.

**Best for:** those wanting to combine Peru and Bolivia on a single journey who are prepared to allocate more time for moving between countries. This itinerary has its own departure, group and accommodation conditions; comparing its price directly with a three-day jeep tour without considering included services would be misleading.

## Considerations on routes through the Siloli Desert

The Stone Tree stands on an open high-altitude plateau. Strong winds, cold and noticeable temperature swings can occur. Warm clothing, wind and sun protection and water are useful. Travellers unused to high elevations should plan their first days particularly carefully.

The three current programmes differ in geography and duration, but the rock is reached on **a vehicle journey through the Altiplano** in every case. The stop itself does not entail a multi-day hike; physical demands depend on the other activities on the selected trip. Access to roads varies with weather and local conditions.

For more about the region, see the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) pages. Other itineraries can be compared in the [Bolivia tours catalogue](/bolivia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Stone Tree tours

### Where is the Stone Tree?

In the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) of southwestern Bolivia, near highland routes through Eduardo Avaroa Reserve. It is a rock formation, not a petrified trunk from a real tree.

### Which tour is the shortest?

Of the confirmed Ada Tours programmes with a mandatory Stone Tree stop, the shortest is the [three-day group jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). It covers lagoons, volcanic areas and Uyuni. Check the starting point: the trip begins at Hito Cajones.

### Can the Stone Tree and Laguna Colorada be visited together?

Yes. All three listed programmes include both the [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) in their highland stages. Each tour page gives the precise order.

### Which should I choose to see Machu Picchu too?

The [15-day Peru and Bolivia tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/). The other two programmes in this selection focus on Bolivia and do not include Machu Picchu.

### Do you need a separate day for the rock?

None of the published programmes allocates a whole day exclusively to the rock: it lies between other Altiplano sights. Plan around the full route and driving time, rather than one photography stop.

## Chantani Museum near Uyuni: life on the Altiplano and stone figures

Chantani Museum (Museo de Chantani) lies in the Bolivian highlands near the northern part of [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). This small local museum introduces the culture of communities around [Tunupa Volcano](/bolivia/place/tunupa-volcano/). It adds objects from everyday life to a journey through the salt flat's landscapes.

Local tourist descriptions mention old and more recent crockery, kitchen utensils, clothing and farming tools in the collection. A second area presents stone figures of animals displayed outdoors. This makes the museum **a cultural stop**, rather than merely a place for a brief photograph against the salt flat.

## What you can see inside and outdoors

The indoor displays illustrate the lives of Altiplano communities: food preparation, agriculture and the use of materials familiar in the region. Objects come from different periods, so a local guide's explanations can be valuable if guiding is part of your itinerary.

Outside stand stone representations of animals. Local descriptions sometimes refer to the area as a kind of stone zoo. These are **made or assembled stone forms**, not living animals. They should not be presented as palaeontological finds without verified provenance for a particular exhibit.

Open galleries, display access and photography rules can change. Confirm museum access if you plan a separate drive specifically to visit it.

## Where Chantani is and what lies nearby

Chantani lies around [Tahua](/bolivia/place/tahua/) and [Coquesa](/bolivia/place/coquesa/), on the northern side of Uyuni. Tunupa Volcano rises above this part of the salt flat. The route shifts from a level white expanse to settlements, rocky roads and mountain slopes.

Nearby stops have different themes:

- [Tahua](/bolivia/place/tahua/) introduces life in a small salt-flat settlement.
- [Coquesa](/bolivia/place/coquesa/) provides a starting point for exploring Tunupa's northern slopes; several archaeological places are known in the area.
- [Tunupa Volcano](/bolivia/place/tunupa-volcano/) is notable for colourful slopes and panoramas over the salt flat.
- Chantani Museum mainly tells the story of the people and cultural heritage of the region.

A museum excursion does not automatically include a volcano ascent or a visit to the cave with mummies near Coquesa. Each requires separate arrangements and time.

## Combining the museum with a salt-flat journey

Chantani works best as part of a longer Uyuni trip. On the salt flat, travellers learn about salt production in [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and the natural landscape of [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/); to the north are communities around Tunupa. These are different themes: salt production, nature and local culture.

On our [12-day Peru and Bolivia journey through Uyuni](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), Chantani Museum is scheduled for day 8. The itinerary combines a flight from La Paz to Uyuni, a stop in Colchani, visits to Chantani and Incahuasi, lunch on the salt flat and an evening sunset excursion. This is the confirmed schedule for this particular route, not a universal plan for every Uyuni trip.

When selecting the journey, ask how much time is allocated to the museum and which roads will be used. Transfers across the northern area can take much of the day, especially as salt-flat conditions change.

## Season, altitude and travel conditions

Northern Uyuni is at high elevation. Sunshine and wind can be strong by day, while temperatures fall noticeably after sunset. Bring sun protection, warm clothes, water and comfortable shoes for short walks.

The dry season generally makes driving on the salt flat and roads along its northern edge easier to arrange. In the rainy season, beautiful water reflections can coincide with restrictions on vehicle access. Conditions on the day, not merely the calendar month, determine accessibility.

The museum is small and remote from major cities. Before travelling, **confirm that it can be visited, its opening hours and whether a local guide is required**. There is no universal visiting schedule covering all tours.

## Frequently asked questions about Chantani Museum

### Where is Chantani Museum?

Near [Tahua](/bolivia/place/tahua/) and [Coquesa](/bolivia/place/coquesa/), by the northern edge of Uyuni Salt Flat in Bolivia. It is usually visited on routes through the Tunupa Volcano area.

### What exhibits does the museum have?

Local descriptions mention crockery, clothing, agricultural tools and stone animal figures. Confirm which parts of the collection are currently accessible before visiting.

### Are Chantani Museum and the Coquesa mummies the same site?

No. The museum explores local culture and everyday life, while the archaeological cave containing mummies is associated with the Coquesa area. Visiting one does not automatically include the other.

### Which Ada Tours tour includes Chantani?

It is on the itinerary of the [12-day Peru and Bolivia tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) alongside other stops on Uyuni Salt Flat.
